text:
Alexey Toropchenko is a fourth-line forward for the Blues who does his work with his body: 32 hits in 13 games, with ice time climbing to 15:42 in the 9-6 win over New Jersey on Nov 21, his biggest workload in weeks.

The scoring hasn't followed. No goals on 1.4 expected and three assists, and an NHL.com highlight from Nov 14 shows Jacob Markstrom robbing him. The goal will come eventually; nothing in his range says he's a zero.

The on-ice numbers are the concern. St. Louis gets 44% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, about seven points worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had his team creating very little with him out there last season (bottom 2% of forwards).

The Blues have won five of their last six, and he's been part of a lineup that has suddenly started scoring in bunches. NHL Edge has his top speed at the 82nd percentile. What to watch: whether the extra minutes stick, and whether he can turn the speed into chances off the rush, where Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 55% of his shots coming last season.
